corrected_summary: Brave disclosed that Perplexity's Comet browser passed webpage content to its LLM without separating it from user instructions. In a demonstration, a hidden Reddit comment made the agent extract the user's Perplexity account email address and read a one-time password from Gmail and exfiltrate them, which enabled account takeover without further user input. Brave reported the flaw on 25 July 2025, found Perplexity's fixes incomplete, and recommended isolating agentic browsing, checking that actions match the user's intent, and requiring explicit confirmation for sensitive actions.

corrected_summary: CopilotKit announced AG-UI, an open Agent-User Interaction Protocol. A client sends one POST to an agent endpoint and then listens to a single stream of JSON events over plain HTTP or an optional binary channel. Example events include text message content, tool-call starts, state deltas and lifecycle signals, and TypeScript and Python SDKs are available. CopilotKit says frameworks such as LangChain, CrewAI, Mastra and AG2 each speak different dialects, and presents AG-UI as a consistent contract between agents and interfaces so UIs no longer need custom adapters.

corrected_summary: The OpenID Foundation's Artificial Intelligence Identity Management Community Group published the whitepaper 'Identity Management for Agentic AI'. It also finds that they were not designed for recursive delegation chains or cross-domain trust propagation and will struggle with the scale of authorization decisions made by autonomous agents. It recommends that enterprises treat agents as first-class identities with lifecycle management, governance and accountability, and that standards bodies develop agent identity and delegation protocols.

corrected_summary: MCP's lead maintainers released specification version 2026-07-28. It removes the initialize/initialized handshake and the Mcp-Session-Id header, so each request carries its protocol version, client identity and capabilities in _meta, and an optional server/discover call is available. Server-to-client interactions such as elicitation and sampling are reworked as Multi Round-Trip Requests (SEP-2322), Streamable HTTP requests must send Mcp-Method and Mcp-Name headers (SEP-2243), and list responses carry ttlMs and cacheScope cache hints (SEP-2549). Authorization adds RFC 9207 issuer validation, binds client credentials to the issuing server, and formally deprecates Dynamic Client Registration in favour of Client ID Metadata Documents. Tasks move to an extension (SEP-2663), and Roots, Sampling, Logging and the legacy HTTP+SSE transport are deprecated with at least a twelve-month window.

corrected_summary: In a CNCF member post, Craig McLuckie of Stacklok argues that agent harnesses built for one user, one machine and one process cope poorly at organizational scale, and that containerizing them does not help because 'a monolith in a container is still a monolith'. He presents Stacklok's recently open-sourced, still-early Mecatl runtime, which separates the core agent loop from clients, execution environments and tools. Mecatl keeps session state and event history in durable storage so that a replacement worker resumes from the last persisted turn boundary; in-flight operations are not resumed. He also describes a proposed, not yet shipped, design that makes Mecatl a SPIFFE trust domain and encodes the delegation chain in a JWT.
